messages:
Anna Li: incident-bot just fired for sustained node disk writeback and pod churn in us-east-1-gpu-cluster. dashboards show rapid /tmp growth and modelcache evictions, a bunch of runtimes OOMKilled. Paging oncall.
Incident Bot: ALERT: node.fs.writeback_high > 95% on nodes: gpu-32a,gpu-32b,gpu-33c. 35 pods with eviction_score >= 0.9. Pager: @Jordan (oncall-sre)
Jordan (oncall-sre): taking it. grabbing logs. initial hypothesis: runaway log spool + modelcache temp files filling tmpfs during parallel model loads.
Raj Patel: seeing CUDA init failures from one of the restarts: "CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY" in serve-runtime logs, but the host rootfs is at 96%. probably container crash due to combined memory + disk pressure.
Kai Nguyen: adding context — we rolled the new modelcache prefetch change ~45m ago that writes temporary shard indexes to /tmp before move. Could be the change + increased traffic.
Anna Li: customer impact: A/B tests show 502s for ~7% of requests hitting the large-ctx models. Fallbacks triggered but increased tail latency. Oncall, please call out customer-facing impact in the next update.
Jordan (oncall-sre): doing triage checklist: 1) isolate nodes 2) reduce prefetch concurrency 3) free tmp 4) restart affected pods. Starting with temporary mitigation: cordon gpu-32a/gpu-32b; will scale down modelcache prefetch on route.
Maria Gomez: ETA on cordon/drain? I can take rollback for the prefetch change if we need.
Jordan (oncall-sre): cordon done for gpu-32a/gpu-32b (kubectl cordon). Not draining to avoid mass restarts; will cordon then ssh to clear /tmp on remaining nodes.
Jordan (oncall-sre): running cleanup on gpu-33c: 
```bash
ssh gpu-33c sudo du -sh /tmp/* | sort -h | tail -n 20
sudo rm -rf /tmp/modelcache_temp_* /tmp/log-spool-*
systemctl restart serve-runtime
```
Raj Patel: paste of recent container log snippet: 
```
[2026-03-15T10:12:03Z] serve-runtime ERROR: kvcache write failed: No space left on device
[2026-03-15T10:12:04Z] serve-runtime FATAL: OOMKilled during model load
[2026-03-15T10:12:05Z] kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 2345 (serve-runtime)
[2026-03-15T10:12:06Z] nvidia: GPU init failed: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
```
Kai Nguyen: I decreased prefetch concurrency on the canary config for large-ctx to 2 -> 1 via console, request routing updated. Hoping that reduces temp file churn.
Incident Bot: ACTION: Rollout change detected: modelcache-prefetch concurrency reduced on route /v1/generate-large from 4 -> 1 by Kai Nguyen.
Anna Li: Jordan — how many pods restarted so far and what's remaining affected?
Jordan (oncall-sre): ~18 pods restarted, 9 still in CrashLoopBackOff. After manual /tmp purge on three nodes, two came back. One node still shows kernel writeback saturation, investigating disk write IO.
Maria Gomez: if we can't stabilize quickly, we should rollback prefetch change. I can prepare a rollback patch, but prefer to avoid full rollback if concurrency tweak works.
Raj Patel: to reduce blast radius, paused autoscaler for the affected nodepool and bumped eviction threshold on policy to prefer killing non-critical sidecars first. Applied with: 
```yaml
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: EvictionPolicy
spec:
  priorityOrder: [sidecar, cache-preload, main]
  threshold: 0.97
```
Jordan (oncall-sre): customer impact update: ~4% of requests for large-ctx still falling back, some latency spikes reported. No account-wide outage, but higher error rate for heavy model routes. Notifying support to prepare tickets.
Anna Li: assigning followups: Jordan to continue node cleanup and triage (oncall). Kai to monitor canary and metrics (throughput, tmpfs usage, CUDA errors). Raj to prepare postmortem template and collect logs. Maria to stand by for rollback. I'll update exec and CSMs in 30.
Jordan (oncall-sre): started background job to collect /var/log/journal and docker logs, and saved node snapshots. uploaded to https://internal.redwood/incident/1977777000/artifacts (logs and graphs).
deploy-bot: Deploy notice: rollback available for modelcache-prefetch @ rollback/2026-03-15-01 if needed.
Kai Nguyen: metric check 10m after concurrency reduction: tmpfs usage down by ~40% on affected nodes, eviction events reduced. CUDA errors still present on two hosts; will attempt coordinated restart after I/O stabilizes.
Maria Gomez: proceeding with staged rollback prep just in case. tagging prod-sre for watch.
Jordan (oncall-sre): handoff note for next oncall (ETA 1h): nodes gpu-33c/gpu-34a require disk fsck scheduled, continue watching tmpfs and eviction counts, if eviction_score > 0.95 escalate to infra for kernel mount options.
Anna Li: thanks team. next update in 30 or earlier if customer impact worsens. :thumbsup:
